featured.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程与访谈创作者
featured.summaryEn: Peter Yang made a pointed call this week: banning Chinese models would be the same self-own as banning Chinese EVs—looks protective short-term, only leaves you behind long-term. He also relayed Thariq's take on AI content review: for non-deterministic tasks like "is this a good video short," don't let the working agent judge itself. Use a separate verification agent reading a rubric. The reason is self-preferential bias—models are more lenient when grading their own output.
featured.insightZh: Peter Yang 这周抛出一个挺有争议的判断：封禁中国模型会像当年封禁中国电动车一样，是一次典型的「自伤式操作」——短期看着像保护，长期只会让自己落后。他还转述了 Thariq 关于 AI 内容评审的观点：像「这条短视频到底好不好」这种没有确定答案的任务，不能让干活的 agent 自己判断，得单独派一个验证 agent 拿着评分标准（rubric）来审。原因是「自偏好偏差」——模型倾向于偏袒自己的输出，自己审自己会更宽松。

featured.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人）
featured.summaryEn: Madhu Guru offered a grounded framing of AGI: "The road to AGI is paved with economically valuable tasks." That's why enterprise AI is one of the most important frontiers—it's where many of those tasks live. He also had a sharp observation: four years after peak web3 crypto tokenomics debates, the tokenomics debate that actually matters is open vs closed weights, inference costs, and model routing. And he argued it's "literally the greatest time ever to have product sense."
featured.insightZh: Madhu Guru 给 AGI 下了个务实的定义：「通往 AGI 的路，是由一件件有经济价值的任务铺成的。」他认为这正是企业级 AI 之所以是最重要前沿的原因——大量真正有价值的任务都活在企业场景里。他还有个犀利观察：web3 和加密货币的 tokenomics 争论吵了四年，结果真正重要的「token 经济学」是开源 vs 闭源权重、推理成本和模型路由。此外他直言现在「是有史以来产品 sense 最值钱的时候」。

featured.title: Booking.com CEO Glenn Fogel 谈 AI 时代的旅行
featured.summaryEn: There is no moat that protects you from innovation forever—the only way to win long-term is to develop new services every day and do your customers' business better. Glenn Fogel is CEO of Booking Holdings, who joined in 2000 when it was just Priceline worth a few hundred million, and helped grow it into a hundred-billion-dollar travel giant. He drew a direct parallel between the dot-com bubble and today's AI wave: roughly 1,500 companies went public in 1999-2000, of which maybe two dozen survive. He won't predict this cycle's success ratio but is certain "there'll be a great deal of disappointment, a lot of people will lose a lot of money—that's just how our economy works." On travel plus AI, he treats AI as a powerful tool to amplify the company's mission. He personally used Priceline's agent system Penny to plan a complex family Europe trip—two cabins, one person branching to another…
featured.insightZh: 没有什么护城河能永远保护你不被创新颠覆——唯一的长期赢法是每天都在开发新服务、把客户的事做得更好。 Glenn Fogel 是 Booking Holdings 的 CEO，2000 年公司还叫 Priceline、只值几亿美元时他就加入了，如今把它做成了千亿美元级的旅行巨头。他把当年互联网泡沫和今天的 AI 浪潮做了直接对比：1999 到 2000 年有约 1500 家公司上市，最后只剩下两打左右活着。他不预测这轮 AI 的成败比例，但笃定「会有大量失望，很多人会亏很多钱，这就是经济运行的方式」。 关于旅行 + AI，他的态度是把 AI 当成放大自身使命的强力工具。他亲身试用了 Priceline 的 agent 系统 Penny 来规划一次复杂的家庭欧洲行——两个舱位、中途有人要去别的城市、还要算清用积分还是付现——他形容体验「太棒了」。Penny 的采用量过去几个月每月翻倍，带来了转化提升、搜索更快、取消率更低。但他坦诚现在绝对量还很小，还没显著体现在业绩里，而且成本、token 经济学、ROI 和长期客户价值都还在摸索。 关于就业冲击，他最担心的不是技术替代本身（这在历史上一直发生），而是变化的速度——岗位消失和新岗位创造的速率可能不匹配，以及那些无法转型的人（他反复提到「一个 50 岁的卡车司机」）。他在自己公司做的是持续给员工做 AI 技能培训，并呼吁社会更坦诚地讨论如何应对这些变化。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie championed multi-model agentic systems as the future, citing Cursor's new research: a frontier model as planner/orchestrator paired with a cheaper workhorse model can materially lower total token cost, yielding a 15X improvement. He quoted Cursor: "Few moments in a large task genuinely require frontier intelligence—the original decomposition, design decisions, certain trade-offs. Once a frontier planner has collapsed the ambiguity into detailed, explicit instructions, less expensive models simp…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 力挺多模型 agent 系统是未来，并援引 Cursor 的最新研究：用前沿模型做规划和编排、再用便宜的「主力马」模型执行，能把整个项目的 token 总成本大幅拉低，实现 15 倍成本改善。他引用 Cursor 的话：「一个大任务里真正需要前沿智能的时刻很少——最初的任务拆解、设计决策、某些权衡取舍。一旦前沿规划者把模糊性收敛成明确指令，便宜模型只需照做。」他判断这会成为复杂 agent 的核心设计范式：谁越懂领域、越会玩多层级模型，谁就能在编码、金融、法律、医疗、生命科学等领域拿下原本因太贵而部署不了的大工作负载。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch dropped a minimalist but piercing observation: the big lesson from AI is that everything is code. A slide deck is code. Design is code. That cool promo video? Code. Excel automation? Code. The universe? Probably made of code too. The tweet drew 4,300+ likes, hitting the collective realization that generative tools are reframing every workflow as code.
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 抛出一句极简却有穿透力的观察：AI 给我们最大的启示是——一切皆代码。幻灯片是代码，设计是代码，那个炫酷的宣传视频是代码，Excel 自动化是代码，「宇宙大概也是代码做的」。这条推文获得 4300+ 赞，戳中了当下用生成式工具重构一切工作流的集体共识。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder（Follow Builders 作者）
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang shared two observations on AI-native organizations this week. First, if hiring today she'd structure interviews as: Round 1 in-person with no AI, testing domain expertise on the fly; Round 2 a project impossible to complete without AI, assessing not just the result but the candidate's chat transcript with agents. Second, she sees two kinds of companies now—those built before coding agents (scrambling to retrofit) and those founded after. The latter differ from day one: teams under ten because they genui…
items.insightZh: Zara Zhang 这周分享了两个关于「AI 原生组织」的观察。其一，她说如果现在招人，会这样设计面试：第一轮线下、禁用 AI，现场考察领域专长；第二轮做一个「离开 AI 就不可能完成」的项目，不仅看结果，还要看候选人跟 agent 的对话记录。其二，她认为现在的公司分成两类——coding agent 出现之前成立的（正忙着改造适配），和之后成立的。后者从第一天起就不同：团队不到十人（因为真的不需要更多）、按项目而非部门组织、每个人闭环自己的工作、几乎没有内部会议。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari gave founders a reality check: over the last 18 months, many will realize that "no moats left in AI" doesn't mean "scale and capital" become your main moat. He listed cautionary tales—Webvan, Groupon, MySpace, Yahoo, AltaVista, Blockbuster, Nokia, plus the "zombiecorns" of 2021—each structurally and capital-wise in a strong position, yet ultimately beaten by a company with a better unique insight, or collapsing under its own scale. The needle founders must thread: find a unique…
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 给创始人泼了盆冷水：过去 18 个月很多人会意识到，「AI 里没有护城河了」并不意味着「规模和资本」就能变成你的主护城河。他搬出一串历史教训——Webvan、Groupon、MySpace、Yahoo、AltaVista、Blockbuster、Nokia、以及 2021 年的那些「僵尸独角兽」——每一个在结构和资本上都曾处于绝佳位置，最终却被有更独特洞见的公司击败，或者在自身规模的重压下崩塌。他说创始人要穿的针是：找到一个值得投入 10 年以上的独特洞见，同时又足够审慎，不让资本和规模成为洞见的替代品。
